note: Pancreatic cell-line and patient-derived xenografts stalled on refametinib and trametinib, yet trametinib, pimasertib and refametinib each added nothing to gemcitabine in unselected or KRAS-genotyped patients; the KRAS-driven mouse, run alongside the clinic, reproduced the null.
label: Pancreatic cancer (MEK1/2)

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level read; open-access full text not read.
engagement.model: Pancreatic and other tumour xenografts (cell-line, orthotopic and patient-derived)
engagement.note: Refametinib's downstream ERK-pathway signalling was read by western blot in three orthotopic primary pancreatic xenografts; no human comparison yet.
engagement.short: pERK readout in orthotopic pancreatic PDX
engagement.quote: Effects on cell cycle and downstream signalling were examined by flow cytometry and western blot, respectively.
engagement.judgement: Opener for the xenograft track with a member drug (refametinib = RDEA119/BAY 86-9766) in pancreatic PDX; selumetinib papers (Yeh 2007) cited by the v2 draft were dropped because selumetinib is not a member of this tile.

engagement.magnitude_basis: tumour pERK H-score change from baseline at day 15 (FDA ClinPharmR, 22 paired biopsies); no model number to scale against
engagement.population: Advanced solid tumours, mixed types (phase 1), not a pancreatic cohort
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level read of Infante 2012 (paywalled). The dose-response of tumour pERK/Ki67/p27 in 22 paired biopsies (Study MEK111054) is taken from the FDA clinical pharmacology review of NDA 204114: 'Higher doses resulted in greater inhibition of pERK and Ki67 and increase in p27'. Subjects were advanced solid tumours of mixed type, not a pancreatic cohort.
engagement.model: Pancreatic and other tumour xenografts (cell-line, orthotopic and patient-derived)
engagement.note: Paired tumour biopsies at 0.5-2 mg showed dose-dependent pERK and Ki67 inhibition, the readout the xenografts used; mixed solid tumours, not pancreatic.
engagement.short: Tumour pERK fell dose-dependently in patients
engagement.quote: Pathway inhibition and clinical activity were seen, with 21 (10%) objective responses recorded.
engagement.reason: Human tumour pERK matched xenograft readout
engagement.judgement: Engagement admits any dosed humans (healthy volunteers count), so the Phase 1 mixed-tumour biopsies score for this context. Paired, not stated: Infante 2012 reports human pERK but does not put a xenograft number beside it; the model side is Gilmartin 2011 (sustained p-ERK1/2 suppression >24 h in xenografts) and the FDA PharmR study UH2008/00051/02, whose xenograft panel included pancreas. A pancreatic-patient PBMC pERK readout for pimasertib may sit in the NCT01016483 results record (posted 2017-06-23) per the v2 check; not verified in this run, and it would not change the status.

dose.model: Pancreatic and other tumour xenografts (cell-line, orthotopic and patient-derived)
dose.note: Mouse plasma refametinib matched the in-vitro target-inhibiting concentration; trametinib's xenograft target (sustained pERK suppression >24 h) was set by Gilmartin 2011.
dose.short: Exposure target set in xenograft mice
dose.quote: Blood plasma pharmacokinetic analyses indicated that RDEA119 levels achieved in vivo are similar to those that produce target inhibition and cell cycle arrest in vitro.
dose.judgement: The track's exposure target is the one the FDA review and Gilmartin 2011 state for trametinib (xenograft pERK suppression over the dosing interval, efficacious at 0.3-1 mg/kg against a mouse MTD of 3 mg/kg); Chang 2010 opens the strip because it is the earliest member-drug pancreatic PDX with a plasma-level statement.

dose.magnitude_basis: steady-state trametinib concentration vs the 10.4 ng/mL preclinical target (FDA ClinPharmR: 'Mean trametinib concentrations following 2 mg QD dosing exceed the pre-clinical target concentration of 10.4 ng/mL over the 24-hour dosing interval')
dose.population: Advanced solid tumours, mixed types (phase 1), not a pancreatic cohort
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level read; the 10.4 ng/mL figure and the mouse MTD (3 mg/kg daily) are from the FDA clinical pharmacology and pharmacology reviews of NDA 204114.
dose.model: Pancreatic and other tumour xenografts (cell-line, orthotopic and patient-derived)
dose.note: At 2 mg daily, plasma trametinib stayed above the 10.4 ng/mL preclinical target across the dosing interval; MTD 3 mg, so the margin held.
dose.quote: Furthermore, mean concentrations in plasma were greater than the preclinical target concentration throughout the dosing interval.
dose.judgement: Stated comparison: the trial paper itself sets human exposure against the preclinical target. Margin (decision 16): the model named a tolerated efficacious window (mouse MTD 3 mg/kg vs 0.3-1 mg/kg efficacious) and humans reached target at 2 mg below a 3 mg MTD, so margin_stated true and same. This is a class-level PK match in mixed tumours; whether it was enough for pancreatic cancer is the 2013 entry.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level read. Walters 2013 (trametinib, five orthotopic PDX, growth inhibition alone and more with lapatinib) and the FDA PharmR study 2010N106611_00 (trametinib in two KRAS-mutant pancreatic xenografts: slowed growth, 'none of the doses was associated with tumor regression') are the same track with the member drug trametinib.
efficacy.model: Pancreatic and other tumour xenografts (cell-line, orthotopic and patient-derived)
efficacy.note: Refametinib alone or with rapamycin significantly inhibited growth in all three orthotopic primary pancreatic xenografts; trametinib did the same in PDX (Walters 2013).
efficacy.short: Refametinib stalled all three pancreatic PDX
efficacy.quote: Agents targeting the ERK and mTOR pathway have anticancer activity in primary xenografts, and these results support testing this combination in pancreatic cancer patients.
efficacy.judgement: Model prediction on this track: single-agent MEK1/2 inhibition slows (does not regress) KRAS-mutant pancreatic xenografts, read as benefit worth testing in patients. Population is 'Unselected' rather than 'KRAS-mutant': no MEK inhibitor is prescribed by KRAS status, the trials enrolled unselected PDAC, and in Infante 2014 only 103/160 (64%) were KRAS-mutant by the assays used, under the 80% bar for a biomarker context.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: primary OS HR 0.98 (null) vs significant growth inhibition in 5/5 trametinib PDX and 3/3 refametinib PDX
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level read (paywalled); all numbers are in the abstract. Registry NCT01231581 (randomised, double-blind, primary endpoint OS, n=160) results posted 2013-09-26, which sets the year ahead of the 2014-06-07 epub.
efficacy.model: Pancreatic and other tumour xenografts (cell-line, orthotopic and patient-derived)
efficacy.note: Trametinib 2 mg + gemcitabine vs placebo + gemcitabine: OS HR 0.98, KRAS-mutant subgroup no different. Combination design: member drug added to gemcitabine, scored on the primary endpoint (OS) under the combination ruling.
efficacy.short: PDX stalled; patients gained no survival
efficacy.quote: There was no significant difference in OS (hazard ratio (HR) 0.98; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.67-1.44; P=.453); median OS was 8.4 months with gemcitabine plus trametinib and 6.7 months with gemcitabine plus placebo.

patient_trials.quote: KRAS mutation-positive patients (n=103) showed no difference in OS between arms.
KRAS status did not influence PFS or OS.
There was a trend towards improved outcomes in patients without detectable KRAS mutations that deserves future investigation.

efficacy.judgement: Paired comparison: Infante 2014 reports the trial, Walters 2013 the trametinib PDX; no primary source puts the two together until Van Cutsem 2018 (next entry). Year 2013 by the registry rule; the v2 draft used 2014. Earlier unselected MEK failures (CI-1040 2004, selumetinib vs capecitabine 2012) are not scored because those drugs are not members. Refametinib (Van Laethem 2017, single-arm phase I/II, ORR 23%, outcomes better in KRAS-undetectable patients) and pimasertib (Van Cutsem 2018, randomised, PFS HR 0.91) run the same direction and are listed in patient_trials. Combination predictions from the same PDX (trametinib + lapatinib, Walters 2013; trametinib + hydroxychloroquine, Kinsey 2019, whose abstract itself states MEK inhibition 'has provided no clinical benefit to patients with PDA') never reached a member-drug randomised readout and are not scored. Rule question 1 (add-on design vs single-agent model) settled by the 2026-11-09 combination ruling: a member drug combined with another active drug is scored on the trial primary endpoint, so contra stands. Refametinib and pimasertib are now their own tracks (xenograft entries 4 and 10; genotype-panel entries 7 and 8).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: no significant OS gain in KPC mice (single agent) vs OS HR 0.98 in patients; the paper reports MEK + gemcitabine 'incrementally enhanced' OS vs gemcitabine, which patients did not show
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level read. The GEMM was dosed with cobimetinib (GDC-0973), not a member drug (product_in_model false). The paper does not cite the trametinib trial in its abstract; the pairing with Infante 2014 is mine.
efficacy.note: KPC mice given a sibling MEK inhibitor (cobimetinib) showed modest growth inhibition and no survival gain, published after the trametinib trial read out. Retrodiction by post-dating (published after the trametinib readout), per the rule that publication dates decide.
efficacy.short: KPC mouse reproduced the null, afterwards
efficacy.quote: Treatment of advanced disease with either a MEK (GDC-0973) or PI3K inhibitor (GDC-0941) alone showed modest tumor growth inhibition and did not significantly enhance overall survival.

patient_trials.quote: KRAS mutation-positive patients (n=103) showed no difference in OS between arms.

efficacy.judgement: Separate track per the run rule: a different system (autochthonous KrasG12D-driven GEMM) with a different prediction (modest single-agent effect, no survival gain) from the xenografts (growth inhibition in every model). Retrodiction call: the paper's epub (2014-11-05) follows the registry posting (2013-09-26) and the Infante epub (2014-06-07), and its framing is against the clinical scene ('several are currently in clinical trials'), so retro, not same; if the experiments are shown to predate the readout this becomes a prospective same. source_calls_it partial because the model gave MEK + gemcitabine an incremental OS gain that patients (HR 0.98) did not show. Alagesan 2015 (epub 2014-10-27, selumetinib AZD6244 in a KrasG12D GEMM, 'MEK inhibition alone was mainly cytostatic', survival extended only by the MEK + PI3K combination) is the same track nine days earlier with a non-member drug and no single-agent survival number in the abstract. The GEMM's prospective combination prediction (MEK + PI3K/AKT) was tested with selumetinib + MK-2206 (Chung 2017), not a member, so it is not scored here.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: phase II primary PFS HR 0.91 (null) vs 'anti-tumour activity in a pancreatic tumour model'
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level read (paywalled). Model side Vena 2015 (CCR, epub 2015-07-30): pimasertib + gemcitabine caused significant tumour growth delays in an orthotopic pancreatic model. The trial abstract only cites the model, so this is a pairing (comparison_stated false).
efficacy.model: Pancreatic and other tumour xenografts (cell-line, orthotopic and patient-derived)
efficacy.note: Pimasertib + gemcitabine vs placebo + gemcitabine: PFS HR 0.91, OS 7.3 vs 7.6 months; Vena 2015 orthotopic model predicted growth delay with the same combination. Combination design scored on the primary endpoint.
efficacy.short: Pimasertib: model active, patients no benefit
efficacy.quote: In conclusion, no clinical benefit was observed with first-line pimasertib plus gemcitabine compared with gemcitabine alone in patients with mPaCa.
efficacy.reason: Xenografts stalled; three drugs, no patient benefit
efficacy.judgement: First scored entry on the pimasertib xenograft track (model side Vena 2015, epub 2015-07-30; no separate untested opener, since one appended after this entry would break the track year order). Year 2017 by the NCT01016483 results posting (2017-06-23). Primary endpoint of the phase II part was PFS; OS secondary; both null.

efficacy.model: In-vitro cancer cell-line panel, RAS/BRAF genotype vs MEK-inhibitor sensitivity
efficacy.note: Trametinib cell-line panel: RAS/BRAF-mutant lines most sensitive; applied to pancreatic cancer as a KRAS-genotype selection hypothesis, not yet compared. Refametinib and pimasertib tracks on this panel (entries 7, 8) carry no separate opener: appended after them it would break year order.
efficacy.short: RAS-mutant lines most sensitive in vitro
efficacy.quote: Potent cell growth inhibition was evident in most tumor lines with mutant BRAF or Ras.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; pan-tumour panel, pancreatic lines not itemised in the abstract. model_filed not checked against NDA 204114 PharmR in this run.
efficacy.judgement: Opener for the only patient-level prediction in the context: genotype picks responders. A different system (in-vitro immortalised-line panel) and a different prediction (who responds) from the xenograft track, so its own track; ex_vivo is the nearest model_kind.

efficacy.model: In-vitro cancer cell-line panel, RAS/BRAF genotype vs MEK-inhibitor sensitivity
efficacy.note: Randomised phase II pre-specified KRAS subgroups by cfDNA; KRAS-mutant patients (n=103) gained no OS from trametinib, so genotype did not pick responders.
efficacy.short: KRAS-mutant patients gained nothing from trametinib
efficacy.quote: Outcomes were independent of KRAS mutations determined by cfDNA.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Whether the KRAS-subgroup analysis appeared in the 2013-09-26 registry results posting was not checked, so year follows the paper (Crossref created 2014-06-07; print August 2014).
efficacy.judgement: The panel predicted RAS-mutant tumours as the responders; the trial tested exactly that subgroup and found no difference, a wrong patient-level prediction. Pairing: the trial cites the RAS rationale but does not set the panel beside its data.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: OS in the KRAS-mutant subgroup (no difference between arms) against predicted genotype-dependent sensitivity

patient_trials.quote: KRAS mutation-positive patients (n=103) showed no difference in OS between arms.

efficacy.model: In-vitro cancer cell-line panel, RAS/BRAF genotype vs MEK-inhibitor sensitivity
efficacy.note: Single-arm phase I/II (n=90): response, PFS and OS were all higher without detectable KRAS mutation in ctDNA, the reverse of the panel's prediction. Single-arm phase I/II with gemcitabine; the patient-level comparison is the KRAS ctDNA subgroup split.
efficacy.short: KRAS-wild-type patients did better on refametinib
efficacy.quote: Overall response rate, disease control rate, progression-free survival, and overall survival were higher in patients without detectable KRAS mutations (48% vs. 28%, 81% vs. 69%, 8.8 vs. 5.3 months, and 18.2 vs. 6.6 months, respectively).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Springer page blocked). Single-arm trial, ctDNA subgroups, unadjusted. Refametinib's own panel (Iverson 2009) states no genotype prediction in its abstract, so the model side is trametinib's panel (product_in_model false). NCT01251640 has no posted results (checker-verified), so registry_date is null; year is the online date 2016-12-14.
efficacy.judgement: Second member drug on the same patient-level prediction, now with the direction reversed (magnitude opposite). Same status as 2014, so strengthens. Own drug track since the 2026-11-09 split, so this is the track's first contra (strengthens false).
efficacy.magnitude_basis: ORR 48% vs 28% and median OS 18.2 vs 6.6 months, KRAS wild-type vs mutant ctDNA

patient_trials.quote: The objective response rate was 23% and the disease control rate was 73%.

efficacy.model: In-vitro cancer cell-line panel, RAS/BRAF genotype vs MEK-inhibitor sensitivity
efficacy.note: Randomised phase II part (n=88): no benefit over placebo with gemcitabine and KRAS status did not influence PFS or OS; third member drug, same miss. Combination with gemcitabine, scored under the combination ruling.
efficacy.short: KRAS status did not pick pimasertib responders
efficacy.quote: KRAS status did not influence PFS or OS.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Registry results (NCT01016483) posted 2017-06-23 per the checker; whether they carry the KRAS subgroup was not checked, so year is the online date 2018-08-09.
efficacy.judgement: Third member drug; genotype again failed to pick responders.  The track never turned: no tier 1-4 source shows a KRAS-mutant subgroup benefiting from any member drug. Own drug track since the 2026-11-09 split, so this is the track's first contra (strengthens false).
efficacy.reason: Three member drugs, genotype never picked responders
efficacy.magnitude_basis: PFS and OS by KRAS status (no influence) against predicted genotype-dependent sensitivity

patient_trials.quote: PFS and OS outcomes did not indicate any treatment benefit for pimasertib over placebo in combination with gemcitabine

efficacy.model: Pancreatic and other tumour xenografts (cell-line, orthotopic and patient-derived)
efficacy.note: Trametinib + chloroquine regressed patient-derived PDA xenografts (Kinsey 2019); patients given trametinib + hydroxychloroquine third-line had no responses (1/10 stable disease). Uncontrolled real-world series with no success bar: scored on response against the model direction under the single-arm ruling.
efficacy.quote: Of the 10 patients with measurable disease, only 1 patient achieved stable disease, and the remaining patients had progressive disease.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed) for both sides. Patient side is a retrospective real-world series (8 on trametinib + HCQ, 5 on trametinib + CDK4/6i), no pre-specified primary endpoint and no control; Witte 2024 (10.1007/s00432-024-05954-5, 13/13 evaluable THCQ patients progressed) repeats it. THREAD NCT03825289 terminated with no results posted. model_filed false: Kinsey 2019 is academic, not in NDA 204114.
efficacy.judgement: Same PDX system, now dosed with the exact regimen patients later received; the model (epub 2019-03-04) precedes both patient series, so prospective. Regressions predicted, no responses seen: contra, same status as the track since 2013, so strengthens. Hydroxychloroquine is a non-member partner, but trametinib is the member drug and the model tested the same combination.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: Xenograft regression vs objective response (0 of 10 measurable patients responded)

patient_trials.quote: In the THCQ subgroup, all patients evaluable for response (13/19) had progressive disease (PD) within 100 days.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: phase II ORR 23% (single arm, tumour response primary) vs significant growth inhibition in 3/3 orthotopic PDX
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Springer paywalled). Primary endpoint from ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01251640 (phase II: tumour response, blinded read; single group); no results posted. No pre-set success bar found at abstract/registry level. Gemcitabine alone gave ORR 18% in the Infante 2014 placebo arm, so the response may not be refametinib's.
efficacy.model: Pancreatic and other tumour xenografts (cell-line, orthotopic and patient-derived)
efficacy.note: Refametinib + gemcitabine, single-arm phase I/II (n=90): ORR 23%. Single-arm trial with no comparator: scored on its primary endpoint (tumour response) against the model's predicted direction, a response, so same.
efficacy.quote: The objective response rate was 23% and the disease control rate was 73%.

patient_trials.quote: Refametinib plus gemcitabine was well tolerated, with a promising objective response rate, and had an acceptable safety profile and no pharmacokinetic interaction.

efficacy.judgement: Track split: Chang 2010 PDX dosed refametinib (entry 1 opens this track). Under the 2026-11-09 single-arm ruling an uncontrolled trial is scored against the model direction; ORR 23% is a response, so same. Combination with gemcitabine scored under the combination ruling.

safety.magnitude_basis: harms in pancreatic patients (NCT01231581 AE tables, trametinib vs placebo arm, n=80 each) against rat/dog target organs
safety.confidence_note: Infante 2014 abstract plus ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01231581 AE tables (results posted 2013-09-26). Model side read from the bundled NDA 204114 pharmacology review. Ejection fraction decreased 7/80 vs 2/80 was recognised only by a mouse echo run after trametinib's own melanoma result (a retrodiction, not credited), hence partial.
safety.model: Toxicology in rat and dog (13-week), rabbit wedge, mouse echo
safety.note: Pancreatic patients were measured, so they set the status (imported-harm ruling): rat/dog skin, GI and lung findings matched rash, diarrhoea, stomatitis and pneumonitis/ILD (3/80 vs 1/80); the ocular miss seen in melanoma did not appear (blurred vision 7/80 vs 10/80).
safety.short: Rat/dog harms appeared in pancreatic patients
safety.quote: Thrombocytopenia, diarrhoea, rash and stomatitis were more frequent with trametinib, as was grade 3 anaemia.
safety.reason: Pancreatic patients showed the predicted harms
safety.judgement: Re-scored under the 2026-11-09 imported-harm ruling: the draft imported the melanoma NDA verdict (ocular toxicity unpredicted, "In summary, animal toxicities were predictive of clinical toxicities except for ocular toxicity."), but this disease's trametinib patients were measured (randomised, placebo-controlled), so their result sets the status. Predicted harms appeared; the unpredicted ocular harm did not exceed placebo; LVEF fall was not prospectively predicted, so partial. Year 2013 by the registry posting. Pimasertib is its own track (safety entries 2-3).

safety.confidence_note: Read from the bundled NDA 204114 pharmacology review text.
safety.model: Toxicology in rat and dog (13-week), rabbit wedge, mouse echo
safety.note: Trametinib rat/dog toxicology (sibling drug; pimasertib has no public toxicology package) opens the pimasertib safety track. Opens at model_first_use_year 2010 (rat 13-week study); the review was public in 2013.
safety.quote: In summary, animal toxicities were predictive of clinical toxicities except for ocular toxicity.
safety.judgement: Opening entry for the pimasertib track on this model (rule 6; tracks split per drug, 2026-11-09 brief).

safety.magnitude_basis: ocular events 28.9% vs 4.8% (randomised phase II); rat/dog studies silent on retina though dog ophthalmoscopy was done
safety.confidence_note: Abstract (Europe PMC) plus ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01016483 AE tables (results posted 2017-06-23). Model side is trametinib's package (product_in_model false).
safety.model: Toxicology in rat and dog (13-week), rabbit wedge, mouse echo
safety.note: Pimasertib + gemcitabine: ocular events 28.9% vs 4.8% (retinal detachment, macular detachment, RVO in the registry tables), a harm the sibling-drug rat/dog package did not predict though dogs had ophthalmoscopy.
safety.quote: there was a higher incidence of ocular events with pimasertib/gemcitabine (28.9% vs. 4.8% for placebo/gemcitabine)
safety.reason: Retinal harm in pancreatic patients unpredicted
safety.judgement: Track split from trametinib: same model, different drug, different patient result. Pancreatic pimasertib patients were measured, so they set the status: retinal harm unpredicted by species that could show it, contra. Year 2017 by the registry posting.
